The transcript

James glanced at the kitchen clock. The five minutes he had offered Emma were almost gone, and she was preparing to leave when Nora spoke again.

“There is another detail,” she said. “I didn't mention it because I can't be sure it matters.”

Emma remained seated. “What do you remember?”

“The car was dark blue, I think. There was a dent close to the rear light, on the left side. I could see it when the car moved under the streetlamp.”

Emma paused. “That's quite a specific detail after fifteen years.”

“It is. Which is exactly why I don't want you to treat it as proof. I may be remembering a different car. I saw one like it outside the community hall more than once.”

“Did you know who it belonged to?”

“No. But I once saw a man beside it after a meeting. His face was familiar because he sometimes attended events organised by the education trust.”

James set down his mug. “Nora, you don't have to go further.”

“I know.” She turned back to Emma. “I believe his name was Reid. I couldn't tell you his first name or what his job was.”

Emma wrote Reid? in her notebook, then underlined the question mark rather than the name.

“Was Reid in the car when Claire got in?”

“I never said that. I didn't see the driver's face. And I don't know whether the vehicle at the hall and the one on the road were the same.”

James leaned against the worktop. “This is how it started fifteen years ago. A small observation became a rumour, and somebody printed the rumour as if it were a fact.”

Emma recognised the accusation. Her old article had connected Claire's disappearance to a personal argument on the basis of a source she had not checked carefully enough.

“I won't publish Reid's name on this evidence,” she said. “But I can look for records from the trust, or photographs from that time.”

Nora opened a drawer and found an old photograph from a community event. There were people beside the hall and a dark vehicle near the edge of the frame. Its registration could not be read.

“My sister is in that photograph,” Nora explained. “That's why I kept it. The car may have nothing to do with Claire.”

Emma examined the image without taking it from Nora's hands. “Would you consider sending me a scan?”

“I'll think about it.”

James walked Emma to the front door. “You can investigate. Just don't make my mother part of another headline.”

Outside, Emma wrote down three separate points: Nora remembered a dent; she associated a similar car with the hall; and she associated a man called Reid with that other occasion. Joining the three points into one explanation would be tempting. But a possible link was not yet a verified chain.

She left with a lead to investigate, not a driver to accuse.
